title: Do We Live in a Post-Truth Society?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: False or incorrect information shared without checking accuracy.
Facts or information that show something is true.
Based on facts, not feelings or personal opinions.
An online space where people only receive opinions they already agree with.
An unfair preference for one side that affects judgement.
The process of verifying whether information is true.
The ability to understand, evaluate, and question information in media.

sentences.en: In a world of social media, fake news, and deepfakes… how can we know what’s true anymore?
sentences.zh: 在社交媒体、假新闻和深度伪造充斥的世界里……我们究竟该如何辨别真假？

sentences.en: The phrase “post-truth” has become one of the defining ideas of our time.
sentences.zh: “后真相”这个词已经成为我们这个时代最具代表性的概念之一。

sentences.en: Politicians lie without consequence, misinformation spreads faster than facts, and many people seem to trust their feelings more than solid evidence.
sentences.zh: 政客们撒谎不用承担后果，虚假信息的传播速度比事实更快，而且许多人似乎更相信自己的直觉，而不是确凿的证据。

sentences.en: As a result, truth itself seems less influential than emotion or personal belief.
sentences.zh: 因此，比起事实或个人信念，真相本身似乎失去了影响力。

sentences.en: In today’s episode, we’re going to explore what it means to live in a post-truth society…. a society where the line between fact and opinion is increasingly blurred, and where it can feel harder than ever to know what is real.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将探讨生活在一个后真相社会意味着什么……在这个社会里，事实与观点的界限日益模糊，而要知道什么是真实的，也比以往任何时候都更让人感到困难。

sentences.en: At the same time, I’ll introduce some new and useful vocabulary, and we will practice our English listening comprehension!
sentences.zh: 同时，我会介绍一些全新且实用的词汇，我们还将练习英语听力理解！

sentences.en: What is the meaning of “post-truth “? The term post-truth describes a situation in which objective facts and evidence become less influential in shaping public opinion than emotion, personal beliefs, and identity.
sentences.zh: 什么是“后真相”？后真相一词描述的是这样一种情况：在塑造公众舆论时，客观事实和证据的影响力不如情感、个人信念和身份认同。

sentences.en: In other words, in a post-truth world, what feels true becomes more important than what is true.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，在后真相世界里，感觉真实的东西比真实的东西更重要。

sentences.en: For example, a powerful emotional story can outweigh scientific data and people prioritize information that supports their existing worldview, even if that information is incorrect.
sentences.zh: 例如，一个强烈的感人故事可以盖过科学数据，人们会优先选择支持其现有世界观的信息，即使这些信息并不正确。

sentences.en: This doesn’t mean we have no truth anymore.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我们不再拥有真相。

sentences.en: Facts still exist. Science still works. Evidence is still available.
sentences.zh: 事实依然存在。科学依然在运转。证据依然触手可及。

sentences.en: But truth has lost its central role in public debate.
sentences.zh: 但真相已经失去了在公开辩论中的核心地位。

sentences.en: It is competing against emotions and feelings and online information, and this information spreads faster and feels more satisfying than the truth.
sentences.zh: 它正在与情感、直觉以及网络信息竞争，而这些信息比真相传播得更快，也更能带来心理满足感。

sentences.en: The idea of post-truth became globally famous in 2016 when Oxford Dictionaries selected Post-Truth as the Word of the Year.
sentences.zh: 后真相的概念在2016年走红全球，当时牛津词典将“后真相”评为年度词汇。

sentences.en: The editors of the Oxford Dictionary noticed a dramatic increase in the use of the term, more than 2000% compared to the previous ye ar.
sentences.zh: 牛津词典的编辑们注意到，该词的使用频率急剧上升，与前一年相比增幅超过2000%。

sentences.en: Of course, lies and propaganda have existed for thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 当然，谎言和宣传已经存在了数千年。

sentences.en: Ancient leaders, medieval kings and 20th century dictators all used false information to influence people.
sentences.zh: 古代的统治者、中世纪的国王以及20世纪的独裁者都曾利用虚假信息来影响民众。

sentences.en: But I think the current post-truth era is different for two reasons.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，当下的后真相时代由于两个原因而有所不同。

sentences.en: First, people now expect dishonesty. Many people, many citizens, assume politicians, influencers, or news sources will twist the truth, will be lying, will be dishonest.
sentences.zh: 首先，人们现在对不诚实习以为常。许多人、许多公民都默认政客、网红或新闻来源会扭曲真相、会说谎、会不诚实。

sentences.en: They are not shocked by misinformation anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们对虚假信息已经见怪不怪了。

sentences.en: Second, people care less about whether something is true.
sentences.zh: 其次，人们不太在意某事是否为真。

sentences.en: Because identity or emotion, maybe your personal values, have become more important than accuracy, the truth doesn’t always change minds.
sentences.zh: 由于身份认同或情感——也许是你的个人价值观——变得比准确性更重要，真相并不总能改变人们的想法。

sentences.en: Fact checking doesn’t always change minds.
sentences.zh: 事实核查并不总能改变人们的观点。

sentences.en: You can show someone clear evidence and they may still prefer the story that fits their feelings.
sentences.zh: 你可以向某人出示清晰的证据，但他们可能仍然更偏爱符合自己感觉的故事。

sentences.en: How did we find ourselves in this post-truth world?
sentences.zh: 我们是怎么陷入这个后真相世界的？

sentences.en: The rise of a post-truth society didn’t happen suddenly.
sentences.zh: 后真相社会的崛起并非一夜之间发生的。

sentences.en: It came from technological changes, social changes, and political changes that have been building for decades.
sentences.zh: 它源于几十年来不断累积的技术变革、社会变革和政治变革。

sentences.en: One of the biggest transformations came with the rise of the internet and social media.
sentences.zh: 其中最大的变革之一伴随着互联网和社交媒体的兴起而到来。

sentences.en: In the past, most people relied on a small number of trusted news sources: newspapers, television networks, or professional journalists.
sentences.zh: 过去，大多数人依赖少数几个受信任的新闻来源：报纸、电视台或专业记者。

sentences.en: They checked information, edited articles, and tried to maintain certain standards of accuracy.
sentences.zh: 他们核实信息、编辑文章，并努力维持一定的准确性标准。

sentences.en: When the internet arrived, anyone could publish anything.
sentences.zh: 当互联网到来时，任何人都可以发表任何内容。

sentences.en: Information started to spread instantly and globally without filters or fact checking.
sentences.zh: 信息开始在没有过滤或事实核查的情况下，在全球范围内即时传播。

sentences.en: This was empowering, but it also created a world where truthful, misleading, and completely false information existed side by side.
sentences.zh: 这赋予了人们力量，但同时也创造了一个真实信息、误导性信息以及完全虚假的信息并存的世界。

sentences.en: Social media platforms have made this problem worse.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体平台让这个问题雪上加霜。

sentences.en: Their algorithms are designed to show users the posts most likely to attract their attention.
sentences.zh: 它们的算法旨在向用户展示最能吸引他们注意力的帖子。

sentences.en: Those posts are usually the ones that are emotional, surprising or controversial, not necessarily the ones that are true.
sentences.zh: 这些帖子通常是那些充满情感、令人惊讶或带有争议性的内容，而不一定是真实的内容。

sentences.en: On top of this, personalized feeds like your TikTok feed or your Instagram feed, create echo chambers.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，诸如TikTok或Instagram上的个性化信息流会制造回音室。

sentences.en: Echo chambers are spaces where people mostly see content they already agree with.
sentences.zh: 回音室是指人们主要看到自己已经认同的内容的空间。

sentences.en: This reinforces pre-existing beliefs and makes it increasingly difficult for people to understand different perspectives.
sentences.zh: 这会巩固既有的信念，并使人们越来越难以理解不同的观点。

sentences.en: At the same time, trust in traditional institutions like governments, political parties, journalists, scientists, and universities has been declining for decades.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，几十年来，人们对政府、政党、记者、科学家和大学等传统机构的信任一直在下降。

sentences.en: Public scandals, corruption and bias have all contributed to this sense that the people in charge of our society are not always honest or reliable.
sentences.zh: 公众丑闻、腐败和偏见都导致了这样一种感觉，即掌管我们社会的人并不总是诚实或靠谱的。

sentences.en: And when that trust collapses, people look for different sources of information.
sentences.zh: 当这种信任崩塌时，人们就会寻找不同的信息来源。

sentences.en: That might mean social media influencers.
sentences.zh: 那可能意味着社交媒体网红。

sentences.en: It could mean a charismatic political figure who sounds confident even when they’re not an expert.
sentences.zh: 那可能意味着一个充满人格魅力的政治人物，即使他并非专家，听起来也自信满满。

sentences.en: When people no longer know who to trust, they are more vulnerable to post-truth thinking.
sentences.zh: 当人们不再知道该信任谁时，他们就更容易受到后真相思维的影响。

sentences.en: Politics has also become more emotional.
sentences.zh: 政治也变得更加情绪化。

sentences.en: Many political movements now appeal directly to fear and anger and frustration.
sentences.zh: 许多政治运动现在直接利用恐惧、愤怒和沮丧情绪。

sentences.en: Slogans like, Make Our Country Great Again or Take Back Control, are powerful, not because they’re factual, but because they speak to how people feel.
sentences.zh: 诸如“让我们的国家再次伟大”或“夺回控制权”这样的口号之所以充满力量，不是因为它们符合事实，而是因为它们说中了人们的感受。

sentences.en: They’re emotional. Many people end up supporting ideas because they align with their identity or their group, not because they’re true or because they’re backed by evidence.
sentences.zh: 它们是情绪化的。许多人最终支持某些理念，是因为这些理念符合他们的身份认同或群体利益，而不是因为它们真实或有证据支持。

sentences.en: Modern media has played a role as well. News organizations are competing for views and money.
sentences.zh: 现代媒体也起到了推波助澜的作用。新闻机构正在争夺点击量和资金。

sentences.en: And the pressure to get more views and earn more money encourages dramatic headlines and careless reporting.
sentences.zh: 获取更多点击量和赚取更多资金的压力助长了戏剧化的标题和草率的报道。

sentences.en: Over time this has blurred the line between journalism, entertainment, and opinion.
sentences.zh: 久而久之，这模糊了新闻业、娱乐业和观点表达之间的界限。

sentences.en: When everything looks like news, it becomes difficult to tell the difference between factual reporting, political messaging, storytelling, and conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 当一切看起来都像是新闻时，就很难分辨事实报道、政治讯息传递、讲故事以及阴谋论之间的区别了。

sentences.en: And finally, psychology makes us vulnerable to a post-truth world.
sentences.zh: 最后，心理学让我们在后真相世界中变得脆弱。

sentences.en: Humans naturally prefer simple explanation and ideas that agree with what we already believe.
sentences.zh: 人类天生更喜欢简单的解释以及符合我们既有信念的观点。

sentences.en: It’s natural. The modern world is complex.
sentences.zh: 这是很自然的。现代世界很复杂。

sentences.en: Many global problems, climate change, immigration and economics, are complex as well.
sentences.zh: 许多全球性问题——气候变化、移民和经济——同样也很复杂。

sentences.en: They’re difficult to understand. So people turn to explanations that feel easier and satisfying.
sentences.zh: 它们很难理解。因此，人们转向那些感觉更简单、更能带来满足感的解释。

sentences.en: Even if they might oversimplify the truth.
sentences.zh: 即使这些解释可能把真相过度简化了。

sentences.en: I’ve talked quite theoretically so far in this episode, so I guess we should look at some real examples of post-truth thinking.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，我在本期节目中谈论得比较理论化，所以我想我们应该看一些后真相思维的现实例子。

sentences.en: One of the clearest examples comes from the 2016 Brexit Referendum in the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 最清晰的例子之一来自2016年英国脱欧公投。

sentences.en: Throughout the campaign, voters were repeatedly shown bold and dramatic claims.
sentences.zh: 在整个竞选期间，选民们不断看到大胆且戏剧性的主张。

sentences.en: Many of which were either exaggerated or simply untrue.
sentences.zh: 其中许多主张要么被夸大，要么纯属虚构。

sentences.en: The most famous example was the message printed on the side of a bright red bus, claiming that the UK sent £350 million a week to the European Union and that this money could be used instead to fund the National Health Service.
sentences.zh: 最著名的例子是印在一辆亮红色公交车车身上的标语，声称英国每周向欧盟支付3.5亿英镑，这笔资金本可以用来资助国家医疗服务体系（NHS）。

sentences.en: Economists and statistics experts repeatedly proved that the number was misleading and wrong, but the emotional impact of the claim had already taken hold.
sentences.zh: 经济学家和统计专家多次证明这个数字具有误导性且是错误的，但该主张带来的情感冲击已经扎根。

sentences.en: It didn’t matter that fact checkers disagreed.
sentences.zh: 事实核查员是否反对并不重要。

sentences.en: The slogan felt powerful. It promised control and financial security.
sentences.zh: 这个口号听起来很有力量。它承诺了控制权和财务安全。

sentences.en: For many voters in the UK, the emotional appeal outweighed the actual truth.
sentences.zh: 对于英国的许多选民来说，情感诉求胜过了真正的真相。

sentences.en: We saw the consequences of post-truth thinking again during the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我们在COVID-19（新冠）大流行期间再次看到了后真相思维的后果。

sentences.en: Misinformation spread across the internet.
sentences.zh: 虚假信息在互联网上肆虐。

sentences.en: False claims about vaccines, miracle cures, government conspiracies, and the origins of the virus circulated everywhere.
sentences.zh: 关于疫苗、奇迹疗法、政府阴谋以及病毒来源的虚假声明到处流传。

sentences.en: It was a struggle to know what to believe or who to believe.
sentences.zh: 想要知道该相信什么或该相信谁简直是一场挣扎。

sentences.en: Even when official organizations provided evidence-based explanations, many people dismissed them, believing instead whatever aligned best with their fears or their political identity.
sentences.zh: 即使官方机构提供了基于证据的解释，许多人还是对之不理，转而相信那些最符合他们恐惧或政治立场的东西。

sentences.en: And now with the rapid growth of artificial intelligence, we face an even more complex challenge.
sentences.zh: 现在，随着人工智能的飞速发展，我们面临着更加复杂的挑战。

sentences.en: For example, deepfakes are videos or audio recordings or images that appear convincingly real, but are created by an AI.
sentences.zh: 例如，深度伪造是指看起来极其真实、但实际上由人工智能生成的视频、音频或图像。

sentences.en: Political speeches, interviews, celebrity statements, news footage.
sentences.zh: 政治演讲、采访、名人言论、新闻画面。

sentences.en: All of this can be created by AI in just seconds.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都可以在短短几秒钟内由人工智能生成。

sentences.en: When anything can be faked, when anything can be made by a computer, people begin to doubt everything.
sentences.zh: 当任何东西都可以被伪造，当任何东西都可以由电脑制造时，人们开始对一切产生怀疑。

sentences.en: So what are the effects of living in a post-truth world?
sentences.zh: 那么，生活在后真相世界会有什么影响呢？

sentences.en: One of the most serious effects is on democracy.
sentences.zh: 最严重的影响之一是对民主制度的影响。

sentences.en: In theory, democratic systems, democracy, depends on informed citizens.
sentences.zh: 从理论上讲，民主制度依赖于知情的公民。

sentences.en: An informed citizen is a person who can evaluate evidence, compare arguments, and make choices based on facts or information.
sentences.zh: 一个知情的公民是指能够评估证据、比较论点并根据事实或信息做出选择的人。

sentences.en: But in a post-truth environment, voters are more likely to be influenced by emotion.
sentences.zh: 但在后真相环境中，选民更容易受情绪影响。

sentences.en: This, in theory, will negatively affect democracy.
sentences.zh: 按理说，这会对民主产生负面影响。

sentences.en: Education also has to adapt. In the past, schools focused heavily on teaching information, dates, facts, and established knowledge.
sentences.zh: 教育也必须做出调整。过去，学校非常注重传授信息、日期、事实和既定知识。

sentences.en: But students need new skills. How to evaluate sources.
sentences.zh: 但学生们需要新的技能。如何评估信息源。

sentences.en: How to recognize bias. How to question what they read.
sentences.zh: 如何识别偏见。如何对所读内容提出质疑。

sentences.en: How to distinguish evidence from opinion.
sentences.zh: 如何区分证据与观点。

sentences.en: Critical thinking and media literacy is now essential.
sentences.zh: 批判性思维和媒体素养现在至关重要。

sentences.en: Without these skills, young people risk growing up, confused and unable to make sense of the world around them.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这些技能，年轻人长大后可能会感到困惑，无法理解他们周围的世界。

sentences.en: And the post-truth era affects our personal relationships.
sentences.zh: 后真相时代还影响了我们的人际关系。

sentences.en: People increasingly associate with their own ideological group.
sentences.zh: 人们越来越多地与自己的意识形态群体交往。

sentences.en: Basically, they surround themselves with people who think like them, speak like them, and believe in similar things.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们身边环绕着那些思维方式与他们相似、说话方式与他们相仿、且信仰类似事物的人。

sentences.en: Families, friends and coworkers can find themselves in conflict because they now live in different informational worlds.
sentences.zh: 家人、朋友和同事可能会发现自己陷入冲突，因为他们现在生活在不同的信息世界里。

sentences.en: Every argument starts to feel like a threat to your own identity, to your own group.
sentences.zh: 每一次争论都开始让人觉得是对你自身身份、对你所在群体的威胁。

sentences.en: Conversations become more emotional and more defensive.
sentences.zh: 对话变得更加情绪化，也更具防御性。

sentences.en: And people start to believe that the other side is dangerous or immoral.
sentences.zh: 人们开始相信另一方是危险的或不道德的。

sentences.en: The result is a society that struggles to communicate.
sentences.zh: 其结果是一个难以沟通的社会。

sentences.en: Can this be fixed? Is there a solution to the post-truth world?
sentences.zh: 这能修复吗？后真相世界有解决方案吗？

sentences.en: One thing I think is really important is improving media literacy and critical thinking.
sentences.zh: 我认为真正重要的一件事是提高媒体素养和批判性思维。

sentences.en: If people learn how to evaluate sources, recognize bias and fact check information, they become less vulnerable to manipulation.
sentences.zh: 如果人们学会如何评估信息源、识别偏见和核查事实，他们受操控的脆弱性就会降低。

sentences.en: Schools and universities all have a role to play in teaching these skills.
sentences.zh: 学校和大学在教授这些技能方面都扮演着重要角色。

sentences.en: In fact, I credit my studies in History with building these skills while I was at university.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我得把我在大学期间培养出这些技能归功于我的历史学研究。

sentences.en: My undergraduate degree, my history degree, was not really about learning specific dates and facts about history, but instead about reading reports, books, journal articles, and other sources, understanding the perspectives and biases of different historians and writers, and evaluating different arguments.
sentences.zh: 我的本科学位，我的历史学位，其实并不是为了学习历史上的具体日期和事实，而是为了阅读报告、书籍、期刊文章和其他来源，理解不同历史学家和作家的视角与偏见，并评估不同的论点。

sentences.en: It taught me to be very critical and also that there is not just one true history and never one true story.
sentences.zh: 它教会了我保持高度的批判性，并且让我明白历史从来没有唯一的真相，也从来没有唯一的故事。

sentences.en: Another important tool is fact checking and verification.
sentences.zh: 另一个重要工具是事实核查与验证。

sentences.en: While technology can spread information, it can also help fight it when used responsibly.
sentences.zh: 虽然技术可以传播信息，但如果使用得当，它也可以帮助打击虚假信息。

sentences.en: Transparency is also essential. Transparency means that you can see inside something.
sentences.zh: 透明度同样至关重要。透明度意味着你可以看透事物的内部。

sentences.en: For example, seeing inside governments or companies.
sentences.zh: 例如，看清政府或内部公司的运作。

sentences.en: In fact, governments, companies and other public figures must be held accountable for the accuracy of the information they share.
sentences.zh: 事实上，政府、公司和其他公众人物必须为其分享信息的准确性承担责任。

sentences.en: When institutions are open and honest, it can help rebuild our trust and reduce the space for post-truth narratives.
sentences.zh: 当各个机构公开诚实时，它有助于重建我们的信任，并减少后真相叙事的空间。

sentences.en: And finally, there is a personal responsibility each of us carries.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们每个人都肩负着个人责任。

sentences.en: Before sharing a story or an article or a video, we can pause and ask ourselves… Is this true?
sentences.zh: 在分享故事、文章或视频之前，我们可以停顿一下，问问自己……这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Where does it come from? Does it appeal to emotion more than evidence?
sentences.zh: 它来自哪里？它是不是比证据更诉诸于情感？

sentences.en: We may not be able to escape the post-truth world entirely, but I don’t think we are completely powerless either.
sentences.zh: 我们可能无法完全逃离后真相世界，但我认为我们也并非完全无能为力。

sentences.en: I believe that facts still matter. Critical thinking still matters.
sentences.zh: 我相信事实依然重要。批判性思维依然重要。

sentences.en: And each of us can choose to slow down, question what we read, and look for reliable information.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都可以选择慢下来，质疑我们所读到的内容，并寻找可靠的信息。

sentences.en: If we can strengthen our media literacy and become more aware of our own emotional reactions, then I think we can start to create a healthier and more informed society.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能加强媒体素养，并对自身的情感反应有更多觉察，那么我认为我们就可以开始创造一个更健康、信息更通达的社会。

sentences.en: But I’d love to hear from you. Do you think we live in a post-truth world.
sentences.zh: 但我很想听听你们的看法。你认为我们生活在一个后真相世界吗？

sentences.en: What sources of information do you trust the most?
sentences.zh: 你最信任哪些信息来源？

sentences.en: Have you ever believed something that later turned out to be false?
sentences.zh: 你有没有曾经相信过某事，结果后来证明是假的？

sentences.en: And what skills do you think English learners need today to navigate misinformation?
sentences.zh: 你认为今天的英语学习者需要具备哪些技能来应对虚假信息？
